shared: The Thunderbird is a heavy battle armor design developed by Clan Nova Cat to address the Clan's chronic shortage of frontline powered infantry. Produced at the Barcella Battle Armor Facility on Irece, the suit entered service in 3086 as the Nova Cats' first independently manufactured heavy armor. Designed as a practical replacement for the Elemental, the Thunderbird prioritized reliable production over technological ambition. The suit earned a reputation as a capable infantry support platform, combining respectable protection with a flexible modular weapon mount that accepted multiple armament configurations.

Clan Nova Cat's Abjuration in 3060 severed the Clan's access to Elemental battle armor production lines maintained by the Homeworld Clans. Ongoing Jihad-era combat losses further depleted the Nova Cats' dwindling supply of frontline suits. Khan Santin West, preoccupied with the Jihad offensives, was unable to address the shortage until 3084, when he tasked a team of scientists, technicians, and merchant caste members based on Irece with developing a replacement.

Early proposals ranged from reflective armor composites to projected ballistic weapons and even a VTOL-capable frame, but West ordered all extras stripped in favor of a practical, production-ready design. The Barcella Battlearmor manufacturing lines on Irece began output early the following year. The Thunderbird first saw action in October 3085, when an Elemental Trinary of the 489th Assault Cluster deployed mixed suits against a combined arms raiding force on Labrea. The new armor outranged and outgunned hostile Inner Sphere battle armor, proving its worth alongside existing Nova Cat suits.

The design remained exclusively Nova Cat property, and inquiries from allied factions including the Draconis Combine were refused. Combine evaluators nonetheless gathered sufficient data from limited exposure to inform development of the Kishi and Oni battle armor designs. An upgraded variant incorporating reflective armor entered service as early as 3089, replacing the vibro-claw to accommodate the added protection.

The Thunderbird II is a mixed-technology heavy battle armor produced at Wayne Station on Shitara for the Republic Armed Forces. Developed beginning in 3133 through collaboration between Clan Nova Cat expatriate scientists and local industrial partners, the suit evolved from the original Thunderbird design to meet Republic doctrinal requirements. The Thunderbird II integrates an Inner Sphere C3 battle computer with Clan-derived construction techniques, creating a networked fire support platform optimized for coordinated engagements.

The Thunderbird II replaces the original's modular weapon mount with fixed detachable weapon packs in each arm. The right arm carries a battle armor LB-X autocannon with ten rounds, while the left mounts an AP Gauss rifle with twenty rounds of ammunition. Both weapons attach via detachable packs, allowing field replacement of damaged or depleted armament. Reflective armor provides 300 kilograms of protection with strong energy weapon resistance. The defining feature is an integrated Inner Sphere battle armor C3 system, enabling networked targeting data sharing across the formation. Integration of the C3 system required substantial redesign to accommodate the technology within the suit's Clan-derived electronics. Basic manipulators replace the vibro-claw, and the suit lacks jump capability, relying solely on ground movement. The dual-weapon, networked configuration makes the Thunderbird II a potent fire support platform at the cost of mobility.

Following Gray Monday and the collapse of the HPG network, citizens of Clan Nova Cat descent within the Republic of the Sphere became an important source of Clan-specification military equipment. Republic Armed Forces recruitment officers near Nova Cat enclaves drew a steady flow of skilled applicants, including technicians and scientists whose talents had not found a home within the traditional Clan caste system.

A cadre of these specialists from Shitara reestablished ties with local manufacturers who had previously collaborated on the Strix stealth VTOL program. When the Nova Cat personnel provided examples of Clan-specification battle armor, the engineering teams requested assistance establishing production on their homeworld. The Republic High Command endorsed the project but required integration of an Inner Sphere C3 system. Merging the C3 technology with Clan electronics proved challenging, forcing both teams to substantially rework the Thunderbird's internal layout. By mid-3134, production began.

The Thunderbird II reached beleaguered Republic forces, though it never achieved the prevalence of the Kopis or Taranis. The Combine's invasion of Prefecture II complicated Shitara's political situation, and the planet's government turned to the local Nova Cat enclave for defense after the Fortress Republic protocols were enacted. Long-term production prospects remained uncertain as parts for the high-end suit grew scarce.

shared: ComStar developed the Tornado power armor (light) suit in the late twenty-ninth century as a covert operations platform for its intelligence service and special forces units. Derived from Star League-era Nighthawk technology preserved on Terra, the Tornado combined lightweight stealth protection with an adaptive concealment system in a package light enough for extended clandestine deployments. The suit gained a reputation as one of the most effective infiltration tools in the Inner Sphere, serving ComStar and later the Word of Blake across decades of covert operations. Multiple variants expanded the design beyond intelligence work into direct combat and logistics support roles.

The G12 retains the full stealth and protection suite of the original P12 Tornado, including basic stealth armor and the adaptive camouflage system that conceals the operator across visual, infrared, and electronic sensor bands. Word of Blake engineers refined the helmet's heads-up display with enhanced sound processing, situational awareness aids, and interface improvements designed to reduce the temptation for operators to remove their helmet in the field. Two connection ports at the waist allow modified energy weapons to draw power from the suit's military power pack, providing flexible armament without dedicated weapon mounts. Armored gloves enable standard infantry weapon use and anti-BattleMech swarming capability. The suit offers no mobility enhancement, limiting operators to foot infantry speed, and each unit requires custom fitting to its wearer.

ComStar developed the P12 Tornado in the late twenty-ninth century as a lightweight powered armor suit for its special forces operatives and ROM intelligence agents. The design drew heavily from the Star League Defense Force's Nighthawk power armor, several examples of which ComStar had preserved on Terra but lacked the manufacturing capability to reproduce. Engineers at Krupp Armament Works on Terra instead created a new suit that captured many of the Nighthawk's stealth and protection characteristics within a lighter, more producible frame. The P12 entered service around 2905 and quickly became ComStar's signature covert operations platform.

ROM deployed Tornado-equipped operatives throughout the thirtieth and thirty-first centuries, conducting intelligence-gathering missions and special operations across the Inner Sphere. Operations against the Draconis Combine proved particularly frequent, though the suit saw service against targets in every Successor State. ComStar maintained strict control over Tornado production and deployment, treating the suit as a classified asset reserved for its most sensitive operations.

The ComStar Schism fractured that control. When the Word of Blake separated from ComStar, significant numbers of Tornado suits fell into Blakist hands. The Word redesignated their captured suits as the G12, modifying the software and user interface to prevent ComStar infiltration while enhancing situational awareness features that encouraged operators to keep their helmets on. ComStar retained its remaining stock under the original P12 "Hurricane" designation. The Blakists put their G12s to dramatic use during Operation Odysseus in 3058, when special forces teams wearing Tornado suits seized control of Terra's Space Defense System ahead of the main landing force and later helped secure the Titan Shipyards.

With the Word of Blake now capable of producing newly built Nighthawk suits on Terra, the Tornado fell out of favor for elite black operations. The Blakists instead expanded G12 production for their marines, security troops, and allied Free Worlds League Military units. Free Worlds Defense Industries began licensed production on Gibson, making the Tornado available outside ComStar or Blakist channels for the first time. The Word also developed two follow-on variants: the G13, which replaced the camouflage system with a modular weapon mount for direct combat roles, and the G14, which substituted mission equipment storage for infantry support operations. Both entered production at Krupp Armament Works on Terra, with mobile production sites suspected of contributing additional output during the Jihad.

Two experimental variants emerged during the Jihad era. ComStar produced the P17 Hurricane, a custom refit incorporating Clan-manufactured stealth armor and a specialized ranged weapon obtained through undisclosed channels. Only a handful were confirmed built. On Terra, the planetary militia organization TerraSec developed the G17 under Dr. Roger Fennault, a protégé of the Manei Domini designer Dr. Devon Cortland. The G17 incorporated Clan-grade improved stealth composites and VTOL movement systems, though only prototypes saw action during Coalition operations to liberate Terra. Republic intelligence later assessed that mass production of the G17 would have significantly complicated the final campaign.

The G13 trades the original Tornado's camouflage system for a modular weapon mount in the right arm, reflecting a shift from covert infiltration to direct combat support. Basic stealth armor provides protection comparable to the earlier models, though the loss of active camouflage makes the suit more dependent on conventional concealment. The David light Gauss rifle configuration offers precision engagement capability at extended range, allowing operators to deliver accurate fire from positions that heavier battle armor cannot reach. The weapon's minimal heat generation suits the Tornado's lightweight frame, which lacks the cooling infrastructure of larger suits. A single armored glove on the left hand retains the capacity for anti-BattleMech attacks and OmniMech transport, though the dedicated weapon mount eliminates the right-hand manipulator. The suit remains limited to foot infantry speeds with no jump capability.

The flamer-equipped G13 replaces the original Tornado's camouflage system with a modular weapon mount carrying a battle armor-scale flamer. Basic stealth armor retains meaningful protection against small arms and fragmentation, though without active camouflage the suit relies on conventional concealment methods. The flamer excels in close-quarters engagements, building clearance operations, and anti-infantry work where its area-effect damage compensates for the single-weapon loadout. Drawing power from the suit's military power pack, the weapon maintains a reliable rate of fire during sustained operations. The G13 platform retains one armored glove on the left hand for anti-BattleMech swarming attacks and OmniMech handhold use. Ground speed remains limited to conventional infantry pace with no jump or VTOL capability, making the flamer variant best suited to defensive positions and prepared assault corridors.

The grenade launcher configuration mounts a heavy grenade launcher in the G13's modular weapon slot, providing indirect fire capability uncommon among power armor suits. Basic stealth armor offers protection against small arms and light weapons, while the loss of the camouflage system shifts the suit's role from covert operations to fire support. The heavy grenade launcher delivers area-effect ordnance effective against clustered infantry and light vehicles, giving squad leaders a suppression tool that complements the direct-fire options of other G13 weapon configurations. Ammunition constraints limit sustained engagements, requiring operators to manage their loadout carefully during extended operations. The left armored glove permits anti-BattleMech attacks and OmniMech transport. Like all Tornado variants, the suit provides no mobility enhancement beyond the operator's own physical capability.

Mounting a battle armor-scale machine gun in the modular weapon slot, this G13 configuration delivers sustained automatic fire against infantry and unarmored targets. Basic stealth armor provides baseline protection, though the absence of the camouflage system reduces the suit's concealment to passive stealth properties alone. The machine gun's high rate of fire and conventional ammunition supply make it effective for perimeter defense, convoy security, and suppressive fire during squad-level engagements. Ammunition weight limits extended firefights, but the weapon's simplicity reduces maintenance burden in field conditions. The left armored glove retains capacity for anti-BattleMech swarming and OmniMech transport. The suit's foot-infantry speed and lack of jump capability restrict tactical mobility, favoring employment in prepared positions or as part of mechanized formations.

The small laser configuration equips the G13's modular weapon mount with a battle armor-scale small laser, providing reliable energy-weapon capability without ammunition dependency. Basic stealth armor maintains protection against ballistic threats, while the suit's passive stealth properties offer partial concealment without the active camouflage of earlier Tornado models. The small laser generates consistent damage output across its effective range, and its power-pack-fed operation eliminates resupply concerns during prolonged deployments. Heat buildup from sustained fire remains manageable within the suit's lightweight frame, though operators must pace their shots during intense engagements. One armored glove on the left hand preserves anti-BattleMech attack capability and OmniMech handhold access. Ground mobility remains limited to foot infantry speed with no assisted movement systems.

shared: The G14 replaces both the camouflage system and weapon mount found on other Tornado variants with a 210-kilogram armored cargo bay designed for mission-specific equipment. Basic stealth armor provides the same ballistic and fragmentation protection as the G13 line, though the suit carries no integral or modular weapons. Two armored gloves allow operators to use standard infantry weapons and perform anti-BattleMech swarming attacks. The cargo capacity enables the G14 to carry ammunition, medical supplies, demolition charges, communications equipment, or other mission-critical materiel that would otherwise require separate logistics support. This makes the suit effective as a forward supply element, operating alongside armed G12 and G13 teams to extend their operational endurance. Ground mobility matches the foot-infantry pace common to all standard Tornado models.

The G17 abandons the Tornado's traditional ground-focused design in favor of VTOL flight capability, giving operators three-dimensional mobility that few power armor suits can match. Compact VTOL movement systems propel the suit at speeds covering over two hundred meters per second, enabling rapid insertion and extraction across vertical terrain. Clan-grade improved stealth armor composites provide the heaviest protection in the Tornado family, well above the basic stealth plating of earlier models. Extended life support allows prolonged independent operations in hostile environments. The suit mounts no integral weapons, relying entirely on infantry arms carried in its two armored gloves. The G17's dependence on Clan-specification materials earned it a poor reputation for maintainability, and its mixed-technology construction makes spare parts procurement a persistent challenge. Only prototype quantities reached the battlefield.

The P17 Hurricane marks a major departure from the standard Tornado platform, incorporating Clan-manufactured basic stealth armor that matches the protection of Inner Sphere equivalents while drawing on superior Clan materials science. The most visible improvement is a substantially enhanced ground speed reaching nearly thirty kilometers per hour, triple the pace of other Tornado models, courtesy of upgraded motor systems. An anti-personnel Gauss rifle mounted in the right arm provides lethal precision at range, making the P17 far more dangerous in direct engagements than its stealth-focused predecessors. A small body-mounted cargo compartment carries ten kilograms of mission equipment. The suit's reliance on Clan components and non-standard parts makes field maintenance extremely difficult, and replacement materials remain scarce outside dedicated ComStar supply channels. Each suit still requires custom fitting to its operator.

The Tortoise II is a mixed-technology assault battle armor developed by StarCorps Industries for the Republic of the Sphere. Introduced in 3134, the quad-chassis design blends Inner Sphere and Clan components into an unorthodox weapons platform built around a hybrid wheel-and-leg motive system. The suit carries its armament in a distinctive split configuration, with a modular turret mount and a detachable weapon pack that can be jettisoned to improve mobility. Earning the nickname "Wheelbarrow" during its troubled prototype phase, the Tortoise II emerged as a durable if unconventional addition to the Republic's experimental battle armor program.

The Tortoise II's advanced SRM configuration pairs an ER medium pulse laser in the suit's detachable weapon pack with an advanced SRM 3 launcher mounted in the modular turret. The Clan-manufactured advanced missile system provides accurate short-range firepower with eight rounds of ammunition, complementing the pulse laser's consistent damage output. At two tons, the quad-legged suit moves at a walking pace under normal conditions, though removing the detachable weapon pack doubles its ground speed at the cost of its primary energy weapon. The Tortoise II carries 350 kilograms of Clan improved stealth armor, granting both substantial protection and reduced targeting signatures. The suit lacks jump capability and manipulators, reflecting its design philosophy as a mobile weapons platform rather than a versatile infantry tool. Its considerable armament gives the Tortoise II firepower comparable to some light BattleMechs, offset by its sluggish pace and the complexity of its hybrid motive system.

StarCorps Industries began developing the Tortoise at their Thetford Proving Grounds facility on Terra under the direction of Dr. Stephen Vance. The original prototype replaced its rear legs with wheels, an experimental approach intended to improve stability and load-bearing capacity for an assault-class suit. The unusual motive system earned the prototype the unflattering nickname "Wheelbarrow" and proved extraordinarily expensive to refine. StarCorps spent years and considerable resources attempting to reconcile the hybrid wheel-and-leg locomotion before Dr. Vance's redesign, incorporating myomer-enhanced shock absorbers on the rear wheels, finally produced a workable platform.

The StarCorps board approved procurement of Clan-grade components from Arc-Royal MechWorks, allowing the rechristened Tortoise II to incorporate advanced weapons systems drawn from designs like the Cuchulainn and Fenrir II. A sole field trial conducted in 3134 demonstrated the suit's durability and considerable firepower, with opposition forces caught off guard by the punishment the prototype could absorb and deliver. The trial concluded shortly before the activation of Fortress Republic severed Terra's communications with the rest of the Inner Sphere. The Tortoise II's ultimate fate behind the Fortress walls remained unknown to outside observers, though Republic officials had expressed confidence that the design would anchor future battle armor doctrine within the Republic Armed Forces.

The C3 configuration replaces the turret-mounted missile launcher with a battle armor C3 system and a pair of light machine guns with fifty rounds each. This loadout transforms the Tortoise II from a standalone weapons platform into a network-enabled coordination asset. The C3 computer allows the suit to share targeting data with friendly units, improving accuracy across an entire lance or formation. The twin machine guns provide adequate anti-infantry capability, while the ER medium pulse laser in the detachable weapon pack serves as the primary anti-armor weapon. The two-ton quad chassis carries 350 kilograms of Clan improved stealth armor, and the reduced stealth profile pairs well with the C3 system's role as a forward observer. Like all Tortoise II configurations, pilots can jettison the detachable pack to double ground speed, though doing so sacrifices the suit's most effective weapon.

The LRM configuration equips the Tortoise II's modular turret with a Clan-manufactured LRM 4 launcher carrying seven rounds of ammunition, paired with the standard ER medium pulse laser in the detachable weapon pack. This loadout gives the suit indirect fire capability unique among Tortoise II configurations, allowing troopers to engage targets beyond direct line of sight when supported by spotters. The two-ton quad chassis limits ground speed to a walking pace under full load, though jettisoning the detachable pack doubles mobility at the cost of the pulse laser. Protected by 350 kilograms of Clan improved stealth armor, the LRM variant is well-suited to providing sustained fire support from covered positions. The stealth signature helps compensate for the suit's lack of speed, making it difficult for enemies to locate and engage before the trooper can deliver multiple salvos of long-range missiles.

The SRM configuration of the Tortoise II mounts a Clan-specification SRM 6 launcher in its modular turret alongside the standard ER medium pulse laser in the detachable weapon pack. This loadout provides the heaviest short-range punch of any Tortoise II configuration, with three volleys of Clan-grade missiles capable of devastating armored targets at close range. The quad-legged assault suit's two-ton frame crawls across the battlefield at minimal speed, a trade-off accepted in favor of the protection offered by 350 kilograms of Clan improved stealth armor. Pilots can jettison the detachable weapon pack to double their ground speed when withdrawal or repositioning takes priority over firepower. Without jump jets or manipulators, the SRM-equipped Tortoise II functions best in prepared defensive positions or slow-advance assaults where its firepower and armor can be brought to bear without requiring rapid maneuver.

The Trinity is a family of three medium battle armor suits commissioned by the Capellan Confederation Armed Forces and funded jointly by the Trinity Alliance. Introduced in the mid-3060s, the program aimed to make powered infantry available beyond the elite formations that fielded the Fa Shih. The Capellan variant, designated the Ying Long, incorporates advanced camouflage technology derived from an outside source. The Taurian Asterion and Canopian Theseus share a more conventional protection scheme, differing primarily in cosmetic styling. All three designs emphasize ground mobility, close-quarters capability against heavier units, and a flexible modular weapon mount that allows field commanders to tailor loadouts to mission requirements.

This upgraded Asterion variant pairs the advanced armor and enhanced close-combat suite with a support particle projector cannon, combining the improved protection and swarming capability of the upgrade program with energy-based ranged firepower. The vibro-claw and machine gun provide the same close-quarters lethality as the rifle-armed upgrade, while the support PPC eliminates ammunition concerns for the primary weapon.

Advanced armor improves survivability over the original Asterion configurations. Ground movement and the lack of jump capability remain consistent with the base design. The energy weapon loadout makes this variant better suited to extended operations where resupply is uncertain, though the support PPC's power demands and the vibro-claw's maintenance requirements make this the most mechanically complex Asterion configuration in the field.

The CCAF Strategios commissioned the Trinity after recognizing that battle armor needed to reach beyond prestige formations. The Trinity Alliance partners provided funding that accelerated development to under two years, fueling speculation that preliminary design work had already begun before the formal program launched. Initial production was handled exclusively by Ceres Metals Industries on Capella, with the Capellan government employing deliberate delays and bureaucratic obstacles to prevent technology transfer to its allies. Both the Taurian Concordat and the Magistracy of Canopus eventually reverse-engineered the design independently, establishing their own production lines through Taurus Territorial Industries on Sterope and Foxx Infantry Systems on Royal Foxx.

The rapid proliferation of the Trinity across three nations gave the Alliance a common infantry platform that saw its first major combat test during Operation Sovereign Justice, where the suits proved capable against comparable designs fielded by other powers. Upgraded variants incorporating improved protection and heavier close-combat equipment appeared during the Jihad, further extending the family's service life across all three member states.

shared: The Asterion mounts a medium recoilless rifle in its modular weapon bay, a ballistic weapon that trades raw damage output for generous ammunition supply and easy field maintenance. Standard armor plating provides protection equivalent to a large laser strike, using conventional materials that Taurian logistics chains can readily supply. Twin battle claws allow troopers to conduct anti-BattleMech swarming attacks and ride OmniMechs into combat zones. Ground speed reaches approximately 30 kilometers per hour with no jump capability, adequate for keeping pace with infantry formations though insufficient for independent flanking maneuvers. The combination of reliable weaponry and low maintenance requirements makes the Asterion well-suited to sustained garrison duty and extended patrol operations where supply lines may be stretched thin.

This Asterion configuration replaces the standard ballistic weapon with a support particle projector cannon, delivering energy-based firepower that eliminates ammunition dependency entirely. The support PPC provides consistent damage at moderate range, though its power draw limits sustained rates of fire. Standard armor protection and twin battle claws remain unchanged from the base Asterion design, preserving the suit's anti-BattleMech swarming capability and OmniMech transport compatibility. Ground movement holds at approximately 30 kilometers per hour with no jump capability.

The energy weapon loadout frees the trooper from logistical concerns about ammunition resupply, a significant advantage during prolonged deployments. The trade-off is reduced flexibility at close range, where the ballistic-armed variant can deliver more consistent damage output per engagement cycle.

The Theseus carries a medium recoilless rifle identical to the Taurian Asterion's standard loadout, sharing the same ballistic performance, ammunition capacity, and maintenance profile. Standard armor plating provides protection against a large laser hit, using conventional materials suited to the Magistracy's industrial base. Twin battle claws enable anti-BattleMech operations and OmniMech transport capability. Ground speed reaches approximately 30 kilometers per hour with no jump capability.

The Theseus is functionally interchangeable with the Asterion at the individual suit level, differing only in cosmetic styling that reflects Canopian cultural aesthetics. This shared combat performance across two separate national production lines gives Trinity Alliance commanders the logistical advantage of parts commonality when operating in mixed formations.

This experimental Ying Long variant integrates a battle armor-scale C3 computer into the suit's electronics suite, enabling real-time targeting data sharing across networked units. The primary weapon is a King David light gauss rifle, a precision ballistic weapon that complements the C3 system's fire coordination capabilities with accurate long-range fire. Mimetic armor is retained, preserving the Ying Long's signature camouflage capability alongside the network integration. Battle claws maintain anti-BattleMech swarming and OmniMech transport functions.

Ground speed remains consistent with other Trinity variants at approximately 30 kilometers per hour with no jump capability. The C3 integration gives networked formations a marked advantage in coordinated engagements, particularly against opponents lacking comparable electronic warfare capability. The experimental nature of the system and its reliance on difficult-to-source components constrains production to very small numbers.

The Ying Long carries a man-portable plasma rifle in its modular weapon bay, an energy-ballistic hybrid that generates substantial damage and can ignite flammable materials in the target area. Mimetic armor provides the suit's most distinctive tactical advantage, allowing troopers to blend with their surroundings and close to engagement range before being detected. This camouflage technology, adapted from designs used by another power, gives the Ying Long a significant edge in ambush and reconnaissance roles.

Battle claws retain anti-BattleMech capability and OmniMech transport compatibility. Ground speed matches the other Trinity variants at approximately 30 kilometers per hour with no jump capability. The combination of stealth and incendiary firepower makes the Ying Long particularly dangerous in urban and forested environments, though the mimetic system adds complexity that complicates field repairs compared to the conventionally armored variants.

text.overview: The Tunnel Rat mining exoskeleton is a civilian-grade suit designed by General Motors for underground mining operations. Introduced in 3055 as part of GM's renewed push into the mining equipment market, the Tunnel Rat gave individual miners a pressurized, armored frame capable of withstanding the hazards of subterranean work. Modular plug-in ports in both arms allowed operators to swap between specialized tools as job requirements changed. The suit earned a reputation for rugged dependability in confined, hazardous environments. The Tunnel Rat II incorporated a more dependable power source and improved electronics, though it remained otherwise identical to the original in both capability and configuration.
text.capabilities: The Armored Glove configuration replaces the standard industrial drill with a pair of armored gloves, sacrificing raw cutting power for manual dexterity. Operators can handle delicate tasks, manipulate small objects, and perform fine detail work that the drill configuration cannot manage. At four hundred kilograms, the suit provides a single point of standard armor protection and mounts a searchlight for visibility in darkened tunnels. The exoskeleton lacks jump capability, limiting operators to ground-level movement at walking pace. Communication equipment and a basic life support system allow extended underground operation, though the suit's survivability in a serious cave-in remains limited by its minimal armor coverage.
text.deployment: Mining crews across the Inner Sphere deployed Tunnel Rat operators wearing the Armored Glove configuration for tasks requiring manual precision. Delicate vein work, sample collection, and equipment maintenance in confined shaft environments all benefited from the glove's combination of protection and dexterity.
text.battleHistory:
General Motors had been a major supplier of mining exoskeletons during the Star League era, but the Succession Wars destroyed the technological base needed to produce such equipment. GM's exoskeleton lines shut down entirely, and the knowledge to rebuild them was lost for centuries. The recovery of the Helm Memory Core in the early thirty-first century changed everything. As power armor technology became accessible again, GM moved quickly to reclaim its position in the civilian mining market.

The Mole series of mining exoskeletons debuted in 3052, but it was the Tunnel Rat in 3055 that established GM as the dominant provider of dedicated underground mining suits. Produced at GM's Kathil facility, the Tunnel Rat filled a critical gap in the mining industry. Strip mining and shaft sinking relied on heavy machinery, but individual miners still worked smaller veins by hand with explosives and hand-held tools. The Tunnel Rat allowed a single operator to work longer, dig faster, and survive accidents that would kill an unprotected miner. Both models saw wide distribution throughout the Inner Sphere, primarily in harsh environments run by larger mining corporations. The suits remained among the most costly equipment available to mining concerns, keeping them out of reach for many smaller operations.

text.overview: The Tunnel Rat III is a thorough redesign of General Motors' mining exoskeleton line, produced at the company's Talcott facility. Heavier and more capable than its predecessors, the Tunnel Rat III offered mining operators a significantly tougher platform with greater survivability in the event of underground emergencies. Its higher price point compared to earlier Tunnel Rat models limited adoption among smaller and more cost-conscious mining operations, but the improved protection and expanded capabilities made it the preferred choice for well-funded concerns operating in particularly dangerous or remote environments.
text.capabilities: The Tunnel Rat III's Armored Glove configuration pairs its upgraded chassis with modular manipulator adaptors fitted with armored gloves. Massing close to three hundred kilograms fully loaded, the Tunnel Rat III is lighter in frame than its predecessors but far better protected, mounting two points of standard armor and an extended life support system designed for prolonged operations in hostile atmospheres. A basic jump jet system provides thirty meters of vertical mobility, allowing operators to reach elevated work sites or escape flooded shaft sections. The trade-off for this improved protection and mobility is increased cost, making the Tunnel Rat III considerably more expensive than the earlier models it supplements.
text.deployment: The Tunnel Rat III's Armored Glove configuration found favor among mining operations in particularly hazardous environments where the improved armor and life support justified the added cost. Operators performed the same precision tasks as their Tunnel Rat I counterparts, but with substantially better survivability.
text.battleHistory:
The Tunnel Rat III represented GM's most ambitious revision of the mining exoskeleton concept. Produced at the company's Talcott factory beginning in 3062, it was a ground-up redesign rather than an incremental upgrade. GM's engineers prioritized operator survivability and operational flexibility, producing a significantly tougher and more mobile platform than the original Tunnel Rat.

The added capability pushed the price well above the earlier models, and many smaller mining operations could not justify the expense. Larger corporations and government-backed extraction projects adopted the Tunnel Rat III more readily, particularly for work in especially dangerous or remote environments where operator losses carried high replacement and liability costs. The Tunnel Rat III chassis later attracted attention from military planners during the Jihad, who recognized that its modular hardpoints could accept light weaponry with minimal modification.

Heavier and more capable than its predecessors, the Tunnel Rat III offered mining operators a significantly tougher platform with greater survivability in the event of underground emergencies. Its higher price point compared to earlier Tunnel Rat models limited adoption among smaller and more cost-conscious mining operations, but the improved protection and expanded capabilities made it the preferred choice for well-funded concerns operating in particularly dangerous or remote environments.
text.capabilities: The Tunnel Rat III with Industrial Drill serves as the heavy production tool for well-equipped mining operations. The drill output matches that of the lighter Tunnel Rat I and II models, though the improved chassis absorbs recoil and vibration more effectively. Two points of standard armor and an extended life support system ensure operator safety during prolonged exposure to toxic atmospheres, vacuum, or flooding. Jump jets capable of thirty-meter leaps give operators access to elevated work faces that earlier Tunnel Rat models could not reach without scaffolding or lift equipment. The combination of drilling capability and vertical mobility makes this configuration the most productive in the Tunnel Rat line.
text.deployment: The Tunnel Rat III with Industrial Drill served as the primary production tool for well-funded mining operations working dangerous or remote claims. The suit's jump capability allowed operators to reach elevated work faces that earlier Tunnel Rat models could not access without scaffolding or lift equipment.

text.overview: The Tunnel Rat IV is an armed derivative of the Tunnel Rat III, developed by General Motors during the Jihad. While retaining its predecessor's mining-grade chassis, the Tunnel Rat IV mounted light weaponry alongside its manipulators, filling a niche for mine site security and perimeter defense during a period of widespread instability. Multiple configurations offered different combinations of manipulators and light armament. Despite this added capability, the Tunnel Rat IV remained a civilian-grade exoskeleton at its core, lacking the protection and firepower of true battle armor.
text.capabilities: Mounting both a battle claw and a light machine gun, this configuration pushes the Tunnel Rat IV closest to a true combat platform. The light machine gun provides sustained ranged firepower, while the battle claw offers close-quarters defensive capability and heavy material handling. Sixty-meter jump jets, two points of standard armor, and extended life support round out the chassis specifications. Of all Tunnel Rat IV variants, this configuration carries the highest battle value and the greatest sustained combat potential. It remains, however, a mining exoskeleton pressed into a security role, and operators relying on it against dedicated battle armor face overwhelming disadvantages in both protection and firepower.
text.deployment: The most heavily armed Tunnel Rat configuration, the Battle Claw with Light Machine Gun variant was adopted by mining operations facing persistent security threats during and after the Jihad. Operators sacrificed fine manipulative ability in exchange for the strongest combination of close-quarters and ranged defensive capability available in the Tunnel Rat line.
text.battleHistory:
The Tunnel Rat IV emerged during the Jihad, when the widespread disruption of interstellar commerce and the breakdown of local security forced mining operations across the Inner Sphere to provide their own protection. GM responded by adapting the Tunnel Rat III chassis to accept light weapons alongside its standard mining equipment. The result was a family of armed configurations that gave mine site operators a basic defensive capability without requiring the purchase of dedicated military hardware.

Production centered at GM's Kathil facility, and the Tunnel Rat IV found a ready market among mining concerns operating in contested or lawless regions. The armed variants were no substitute for true battle armor in a genuine military engagement, but they deterred bandits, pirates, and opportunistic raiders effectively enough to keep extraction operations running through the worst years of the Jihad and into the post-war recovery.

shared: The Undine battle armor is a medium-weight underwater combat suit developed by Clan Goliath Scorpion. A direct descendant of the Water Elemental mining suit that spawned all Clan battle armor, the Undine was the first purpose-built military adaptation of the original exoskeleton's aquatic design. Entering service in 3059, the suit gave its operators unmatched combat capability in underwater and amphibious environments. Armed with a dual-purpose weapon system effective both above and below the waterline, the Undine filled a niche that no other Clan battle armor addressed. Its specialized nature limited broader adoption, but for those who mastered underwater warfare, the Undine had no equal.

The Undine centers its offensive capability on a single one-shot LRM-5 launcher loaded with amphibious multi-purpose missiles, allowing it to engage targets both above and below the waterline. An ER Micro Laser mounted in the right arm provides close-range firepower, while a battle claw on the left arm enables material manipulation and limited melee capability. A searchlight rounds out the suit's equipment for low-visibility underwater operations.

Three underwater maneuvering units propel the Undine at speeds exceeding thirty kilometers per hour when submerged, making it among the fastest underwater combatants in any arsenal. On land, the suit is limited to a walking pace. Two hundred kilograms of standard armor provide adequate protection, though this amounts to roughly twenty percent less coverage than the Elemental. The Undine cannot perform standard anti-BattleMech swarming attacks, restricting it to leg attacks against partially submerged targets. This narrow tactical profile limits the suit's utility outside aquatic environments.

Clan Goliath Scorpion had long sought to leverage their underwater expertise into a military advantage. Well before Operation Revival, Scorpion scientists began developing a specialized missile capable of functioning as both a conventional LRM and an underwater torpedo, paired with a combat suit designed to exploit this dual-purpose weapon. Adapting the ancestral Water Elemental mining suit for combat proved straightforward, but the missile/torpedo hybrid eluded engineers for years. When the Scorpions failed to secure a place in the Invasion, the project stalled.

A breakthrough in 3059 finally allowed the Scorpions to complete the design, christened the Undine after mythical water spirits. The suit gave the Goliath Scorpions unchallenged dominance in underwater Trials, though its specialized nature meant most Clans showed little interest in acquiring it. That changed in 3068, when Clan Diamond Shark aggressively pursued the Undine through multiple Trials of Possession. The Scorpions defended fiercely, but the Sharks eventually prevailed on Roche. Curiously, the Diamond Sharks never fielded the suits after winning them. The Federated Suns later acquired Undine suits through Diamond Shark trade channels and used the design as inspiration for their own Hauberk amphibious battle armor.

The Upgrade variant trades the Undine's underwater specialization for land combat effectiveness. Jump jets replace the underwater maneuvering units, giving the suit a ninety-meter jump range matching the standard Elemental. This modification allows the Upgrade to operate alongside Elemental Points in conventional ground operations, filling a fire support role that complements the heavier suit's assault capabilities.

The ER Micro Laser is retained, but the amphibious LRM-5 is replaced with an LRM-3 launcher carrying either four reloads of standard missiles or two reloads of torpedo-capable ammunition. A thirty-kilogram armored cargo bay replaces the searchlight, providing field utility. Armor protection remains unchanged from the base model at two hundred kilograms. The Upgrade sacrifices everything that made the original Undine dominant in underwater combat, but gains meaningful flexibility as a light fire support platform. Its ability to keep pace with standard Elemental formations and deliver indirect missile fire makes it a practical complement to established Clan battle armor doctrine.

The Void is a medium battle armor design produced by Ishikawajima-Harima Battle Armor Industries for the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery. Entering service in 3067, the suit was purpose-built as a scout and light assault platform capable of accommodating operators of varying physical sizes, including the larger frames of Clan Elemental warriors. Built on a heavily modified Kage chassis, the Void carries improved stealth armor that masks its signature from both visual detection and electronic sensors, granting it considerable infiltration capability. Jump boosters provide mobility comparable to lighter designs despite the Void's one-thousand-kilogram mass. The suit earned gradual acceptance within the DCMS after an initially lukewarm reception, becoming a valued component of Combine powered infantry doctrine.

The Draconis Combine Admiralty configuration replaces the standard support PPC with a forearm-mounted small laser, paired with a heavy battle claw on the opposite arm. This combination prioritizes close-quarters lethality over ranged firepower, reflecting the tight confines of shipboard and station combat where the PPC's bulk is a liability. Most DCA marines supplement their laser with a right-hand assault rifle loaded with accelerated energy transfer rounds, minimizing damage to critical ship systems during boarding actions. The heavy battle claw makes the DCA variant particularly dangerous in cramped corridors and compartments, where troopers can engage both personnel and light barricades at arm's length. The suit retains the standard Void's improved stealth armor and jump capability, allowing marines to exploit zero-gravity environments and vertical shafts that conventional infantry cannot easily navigate. Reduced ranged capability remains the primary trade-off, leaving DCA troopers at a disadvantage in open-field engagements.

The Void emerged from a prolonged Draconis Combine battle armor development program. Following successes with the Kage, Raiden, and Kanazuchi, the DCMS committed to expanding powered infantry capability, but resistance to non-BattleMech units delayed progress. Operation Bulldog and the Combine-Ghost Bear War forced resource allocation, yet the first prototype did not appear until 3067, five years behind schedule.

Combine scientists built the Void on the Kage platform, modifying it so extensively the two designs bore little resemblance. Accommodation for Elemental-sized operators enabled partnership with Clan Nova Cat, and production authorization followed once the High Command recognized the tactical potential. Ishikawajima-Harima BAI manufactured the suit at Luthien, with additional plants on Agematsu and Loysville opening in 3066. Full production coincided with the December 3067 Black Dragon coup, during which the Otomo and First Genyosha deployed Voids across Imperial City.

The Word of Blake blockade complicated logistics, but outlying factories continued throughout the Jihad. The Luthien plant's dispersed layout on Shizuoka's coastal flats helped it survive the Blakist occupation, and it became the first battle armor factory to resume production after liberation, reaching full capacity by 3079. The Void became standard among DCMS elite commands but remained nearly exclusive to the Combine. The Procurement Department's decision to withhold Minelayer variants from Nova Cat enclaves reflected deteriorating relations with their Clan allies.

The Minelayer is a production evolution of the experimental Caltrop, redesigned with Inner Sphere components after Clan-specification prototypes proved impractical for mass production. Physically smaller than the standard Void, the Minelayer drops Elemental accommodation in favor of a compact frame optimized for its specialized role. Twin torso-mounted mine dispensers carry four minefields each, with munitions tailor-selected at the trooper's base. A medium recoilless rifle provides direct-fire capability against BattleMechs and vehicles that push through the minefields, while a left-arm anti-personnel weapon mount handles sentries and soft targets. Heavy battle claws on both arms allow powerful swarm attacks, and the Minelayer has earned a reputation for capturing MechWarriors and their damaged machines after they stumble through kill zones.

Mechanical jump boosters replace the standard Void's jump jets following an early prototype incident where igniting jets detonated freshly laid mines, killing the trooper. The booster allows operators to deploy mines and bounce clear without thermal risk, though jump distance is reduced. Basic stealth armor substitutes for the original improved stealth plating, reducing cost and production complexity.

Nova Cat second-line troopers found the standard support PPC too bulky for their preferences and replaced it with a left-arm MagShot Gauss rifle, a weapon the Nova Cats acquired from Federated Suns technology exchanges. The Gauss rifle provides comparable range with a flatter trajectory and lower heat signature, making it easier to employ during extended operations. A vibro battle claw on the right hand gives the trooper a lethal melee option, its vibrating edge capable of shearing through light armor and structural materials. This combination of ranged precision and close-combat capability makes the Nova Cat configuration effective across a broader range of engagement distances than the standard variant. The suit retains its improved stealth armor and jump booster, preserving the Void's core mobility and survivability characteristics. The MagShot's reliance on ammunition is the configuration's chief vulnerability, as resupply in the field can be difficult for Clan forces operating far from their logistics chain.

The standard Void mounts a body-mounted support particle cannon as its primary armament, giving troopers moderate range and respectable hitting power against both infantry and light armor. Basic manipulators enable the suit to perform swarm and leg attacks against BattleMechs, and the trooper can ride OmniMechs into battle. Improved stealth armor provides protection equivalent to stopping a medium laser hit while rendering the suit difficult to detect with both visual observation and electronic sensors. A jump booster allows rapid repositioning at ranges up to one hundred twenty meters, giving the Void mobility comparable to the Kage it was derived from despite greater mass. At one thousand kilograms, the Void sits comfortably in the medium weight class. The suit's primary weakness lies in its fixed weapon configuration, which lacks the modular flexibility that many competing designs offer. The support PPC's bulk also limits close-quarters fighting, a trade-off that prompted the development of specialized sub-variants.

Clan Wolf developed the Warg assault battle armor during the post-Jihad period as a deliberate departure from the Clan's traditional emphasis on mobility. Designed from the ground up at WC Site OZ-2 on Tamar, the Warg was built to hold fixed defensive positions against heavy assault, filling a role that lighter Wolf battle armor designs could not. The suit carried a diverse weapon loadout for a Clan design and mounted armor protection that ranked among the thickest in its weight class. The Warg marked Clan Wolf's acknowledgment that shifting strategic realities demanded battle armor capable of absorbing punishment rather than simply delivering it.

The Reactive variant replaces the Warg's standard armor with reactive plating, improving protection against missile and ballistic threats at the expense of the left-arm light machine gun. The shoulder-mounted launchers were upgraded to Advanced SRM-3 racks, providing improved accuracy and damage output compared to the original configuration despite a smaller overall missile footprint. The right-arm small pulse laser and heavy battle claw remain unchanged, preserving the suit's core anti-armor and close-quarters capability.

The trade of the machine gun for enhanced survivability reflects Clan Wolf's operational experience with the base design, where the suit's slow speed often brought it under concentrated fire before reaching effective engagement range.

The Jihad left Clan Wolf's borders under siege from multiple directions. Punitive strikes by Word of Blake forces destroyed key manufacturing infrastructure, and the return of Clan Hell's Horses to the Inner Sphere further strained Wolf resources. Forced to adopt a more defensive posture, the Wolf leadership recognized a need for heavier battle armor to supplement their frontline OmniMech formations. The success of Clan Jade Falcon's Ironhold suit proved the final catalyst, convincing Wolf leadership to invest in a heavier design class.

Khan Ward authorized a ground-up assault suit design program, rejecting outside assistance from Clan Diamond Shark despite repeated attempts to gain access. Development proceeded slowly over six years, with the first Warg suits entering service in 3085. Production began on Tamar, though the line later relocated to Stewart's Corean Enterprises facility as Clan Wolf shifted its industrial base. The Reactive armor variant followed in 3122, reflecting continued investment in the design.

The Warg weighs nearly two thousand kilograms, placing it firmly in the assault weight class. Its primary weapon is a right-arm small pulse laser capable of engaging both armored and conventional targets. Dual shoulder-mounted SRM-3 launchers provide considerable missile firepower, each carrying three volleys of ammunition for sustained engagements. A left-arm light machine gun handles anti-infantry duties, while a heavy battle claw in the same arm provides a close-quarters threat against anything that approaches within reach.

Four hundred kilograms of standard armor give the Warg protection exceeded only by the Ghost Bear Golem and the Marian Ravager. The suit's chief limitation is speed. Moving at just ten kilometers per hour with no jump capability, the Warg depends heavily on armored personnel carriers for tactical mobility, making coordination with transport vehicles essential for offensive operations.

The Wraith is a medium battle armor suit developed by the Rasalhague Dominion at BA Facility Gamma on Mannedorf. Entering service in 3116, the design descended from extensive testing of the earlier Rogue Bear prototype and was built to support conventional infantry forces and conduct infiltration operations. The Wraith's mixed Clan and Inner Sphere technology base reflected the Dominion's hybrid military culture. Offered in a variety of frame sizes uncommon for Clan battle armor, the suit became a practical workhorse for both garrison and frontline Dominion formations.

The Anti-Infantry configuration replaces the standard Wraith's machine guns with a Firedrake Support Needler in each arm, weapons optimized for suppressing and eliminating unarmored personnel. Reactive Armor replaces the Basic Stealth system, trading electronic concealment for improved resistance to explosive ordnance and missile fire. An Improved Sensor suite allows troopers to detect hidden or camouflaged units, making this configuration well suited for sweep-and-clear operations.

The shift from stealth to reactive protection reflects a different tactical philosophy. Where the standard Wraith relies on avoiding detection to close with targets, the Anti-Infantry variant expects to operate in direct contact with enemy forces and prioritizes survivability under fire. The vibro-claws and jump capability carry over from the base design, preserving the suit's close-quarters lethality. The trade-off leaves this configuration more exposed to detection at range, a limitation that commanders must account for during approach planning.

The Wraith traces its lineage to the Rogue Bear, a heavy battle armor prototype first fielded by Clan Ghost Bear garrison forces in the early 3070s. Decades of iterative refinement at BA Facility Gamma on Mannedorf transformed the concept into the production Wraith, which entered Rasalhague Dominion service in 3116. Unlike most Clan battle armor, the Wraith was engineered around interchangeable form factors to accommodate the Dominion's mixed Clan-freeborn military, where standardized Elemental-proportioned suits excluded many otherwise capable warriors from powered armor duty. Quartermasters complained that the variety of frame sizes created a logistical burden, but field commanders valued the expanded recruitment pool.

The Wraith earned its reputation during operations in the late 3130s. In 3137, Rasalhague Dominion forces launched border raids against the Draconis Combine while the Combine struggled with the death of Theodore Kurita. On Schuyler, elements of the Fourth Bear Regulars dropped a Star of battle armor onto the Kurokawa motor pool before dawn and fought building to building for three hours against three companies of conventional infantry. Separately, during Clan-on-Clan skirmishes over worlds vacated by Clan Wolf, two Points of Wraiths led a flanking assault against the Hell's Horses' 666th Mechanized Assault Cluster on New Oslo, intercepting and eliminating the Cluster's command staff during a withdrawal.

The standard Wraith mounts a single machine gun in each arm, supplemented by vibro-claws for close combat, anti-BattleMech attacks, and boarding actions. Basic Stealth armor conceals the suit from electronic detection, while jump jets provide a ninety-meter leap range. At one thousand kilograms, the suit falls in the medium weight class with respectable mobility for its protection level.

The Wraith's heads-up display incorporates an automated threat prioritization system that assigns targeting icons of varying size, color, and shape based on target type and range. Ten user-customizable presets allow troopers to tailor the display to their preferred engagement style. An exchangeable ammunition magazine similar to OmniMech pod technology significantly reduces field reloading time. The absence of modular weapon mounts limits loadout flexibility compared to some competing designs, forcing configuration changes at the factory level rather than in the field.

The Xiphos, named for an ancient Greek double-edged sword, was developed by Irian Technologies for the Marik-Stewart Commonwealth. Entering service in 3116, the assault-class battle armor was designed to protect infantry against artillery bombardment, one of the most effective countermeasures against powered armor formations. Weighing two thousand kilograms, the Xiphos carries specialized protective plating and an advanced communications suite resistant to electronic countermeasures. Three standard weapon configurations offer flexibility ranging from ballistic firepower to thermal detection and area denial. The suit earned a strong reputation for durability and reliable performance across both defensive and offensive operations.

The Xiphos mounts close to a full ton of reactive armor, providing assault-class protection with particular resistance to explosive munitions and indirect fire. A basic manipulator on the right arm allows limited object handling, while modular weapon mounts on both arms give the suit configuration flexibility. The left arm mount carries the greater weapon capacity. An improved communications system allows battlefield coordination even under active electronic countermeasures, a critical advantage for formations operating beyond BattleMech support range.

Configuration A pairs a light recoilless rifle with a Magshot gauss rifle, offering a balanced ballistic loadout effective against both infantry and light vehicles. The recoilless rifle provides dependable antipersonnel firepower, while the Magshot delivers accurate ranged fire with minimal ammunition weight. At two thousand kilograms, the Xiphos sacrifices speed for durability. Its twenty-two kilometer per hour ground speed limits tactical mobility, but the suit’s protection and firepower make it well-suited to defensive positions and deliberate assaults where staying power matters more than agility.

The Xiphos grew out of Irian Technologies’ efforts to address artillery bombardment, one of powered infantry’s oldest and deadliest vulnerabilities. Commissioned by the Marik-Stewart Commonwealth, the suit entered production in 3116 at facilities on both Irian and Washburn. Its reactive armor gave troopers meaningful protection against indirect fire for the first time, filling a long-standing capability gap in battle armor design.

Commonwealth forces put the Xiphos to effective use across numerous engagements during the Dark Age. Militia units on Laureles proved the suit’s communications resilience under electronic warfare conditions in 3118. The Eighth Free Worlds Legionnaires employed Xiphos troopers in a covert 3125 raid on Corey, dropping them directly into Hollis Incorporated’s facilities to seize Catapult spare parts. During the Wolf Empire’s invasion of the former Free Worlds League, Commonwealth defenders repeatedly ambushed Wolf artillery positions using helicopter-delivered Xiphos formations on Autumn Wind and several other contested worlds. The tactic proved effective until the battle for Washburn, where prepared Wolf forces overwhelmed the defenders with battle armored troops positioned behind their own artillery. Washburn’s fall brought one production line under Clan Wolf control, and Wolf warriors quickly adopted the suit for their own formations.

A basic manipulator on the right arm allows limited object handling, while modular weapon mounts on both arms give the suit configuration flexibility.
