Configuration B replaces the ballistic weapons with a plasma rifle and a one-shot short-range missile launcher. The plasma rifle generates extreme heat on impact, forcing BattleMech pilots to manage rising thermal loads while dealing significant damage to conventional infantry and light armor. The single SRM round provides an opening salvo, allowing troopers to soften targets before closing to plasma range. This loadout makes the B configuration particularly dangerous to units that rely on heat management for combat effectiveness. The plasma rifle’s twenty-round ammunition supply provides enough endurance for sustained engagements, and the combination of heat-inducing weapons with the suit’s heavy armor makes this configuration effective in close-quarters combat.

The Xiphos mounts close to a full ton of reactive armor, providing assault-class protection with particular resistance to explosive munitions and indirect fire. A basic manipulator on the right arm allows limited object handling, while modular weapon mounts on both arms give the suit configuration flexibility. An improved communications system allows battlefield coordination even under active electronic countermeasures.

Configuration C takes a different approach, mounting a heat sensor alongside a heavy flamer to create a specialized detection and area-denial loadout. The heat sensor allows troopers to identify concealed units, hidden infantry, and powered-down vehicles through their thermal signatures, giving the formation a reconnaissance capability unusual for assault-class battle armor. The heavy flamer provides devastating close-range firepower against infantry positions, structures, and wooded terrain, with ten rounds of fuel providing adequate endurance for clearing operations. This configuration trades the raw combat power of other loadouts for tactical utility, allowing formations to screen ahead of friendly forces and clear defensive positions at close range.

The Zou is a heavy battle armor suit developed by Ishikawajima-Harima Battle Armor Industries for the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery. Named for the Japanese word for elephant, the 1,500-kilogram design entered service in 3113 as part of the Combine's third generation of battle armor. Built to fulfill a command-and-control role while providing heavy infantry capability, the Zou earned a reputation for toughness among DCMS infantry formations. The design is fielded in both a direct-combat configuration and a variant equipped with battlefield coordination electronics.

The C3 variant replaces the medium laser with a battle armor C3 system, a medium recoilless rifle with twenty rounds of ammunition, and a battle claw on the left arm. This loadout shifts the suit from direct combatant to a command-and-control platform capable of coordinating fire across linked units. The recoilless rifle provides adequate self-defense, while the battle claw enables close combat and field manipulation tasks.

The C3 integration provides commanders with a heavier ground unit for combined-arms operations, allowing troopers to direct artillery strikes, call in long-range fire, and coordinate maneuvers from hardened observation posts. When dug into a defensive position, the C3 Zou is exceptionally difficult to dislodge, as any attempt to close exposes attackers to precisely coordinated supporting fire from networked assets.

The Zou emerged from the Draconis Combine's third generation battle armor program, developed by Ishikawajima-Harima Battle Armor Industries on Luthien. The High Command's original requirement called for a successor to the aging Kanazuchi assault suit, and the initial prototype fulfilled that role with heavy armor plating designed to counter energy weapons. A subsequent development phase added command-and-control electronics, transforming the design from a straightforward heavy combatant into a coordination platform for combined-arms operations.

The suit entered service in 3113 but saw limited distribution for nearly two decades. Deployment expanded significantly in the 3130s as the DCMS prepared for offensive operations against the Republic of the Sphere. With Kanazuchi stocks dwindling, the Zou filled a growing need in heavy infantry formations across multiple frontline regiments. The C3-equipped variant proved especially popular among active combat commands, where its coordination capabilities justified the higher procurement cost. The original laser-armed pattern remained common in garrison and second-line assignments where combat intensity was lower.

The standard Zou mounts a medium laser as its primary weapon, with enough charge capacity for thirty discharges. The suit carries over half a ton of reflective armor, granting strong protection against beam weapons, a quality that made the design attractive to garrison commanders facing energy-weapon-equipped threats.

Ground-bound at 22 kilometers per hour, the Zou trades mobility for staying power. The lack of jump capability limits traversal of broken terrain and prevents vertical assaults, but the heavy armor allows troopers to hold fortified positions under sustained fire. The suit's sensor profile runs unusually low for its mass, making it difficult to track on targeting displays and partially compensating for the slow approach speed. Intuitive controls reduce training requirements, making the Zou accessible to less experienced operators.

text.capabilities: The suit's modular weapon mount in its right arm accepts an AP Gauss rifle with twenty rounds of ammunition, orienting the design toward an anti-infantry role. A vibro-claw on the left arm allows troopers to latch onto friendly OmniMechs and combat vehicles for battlefield transport. Weighing 1,500 kilograms at maximum load, the Thunderbird carries 250 kilograms of standard armor, providing protection comparable to the Elemental it was designed to replace. A jump booster supplements the suit's ground speed, giving troopers limited aerial mobility for repositioning and terrain traversal. The heavy chassis design makes the Thunderbird less effective in the anti-BattleMech swarming attacks that earned the Elemental its fearsome reputation, but its superior mobility compared to most heavy suits and generous payload capacity partially offset this limitation.
text.deployment: ComStar and Word of Blake forces organized captured Thunderbird suits into six-trooper Level I formations consistent with their military doctrine. Acquisition of these Clan-produced suits required either battlefield salvage or indirect procurement, as the Nova Cats refused to share the design with any outside organization.

Inner Sphere operators fielding the ER Laser configuration in four-trooper squads valued its ammunition independence for extended patrol operations. Combine units that obtained small numbers of Thunderbirds through irregular channels favored the energy weapon loadout for garrison duty where resupply was uncertain.

Nova Cat Points equipped with the ER Laser configuration typically drew defensive and patrol assignments where sustained operations made ammunition-free weapons preferable. Five-trooper Points rotated between energy and ballistic loadouts depending on mission requirements, taking advantage of the Thunderbird's modular weapon mount.

Level I formations employing the ER Laser configuration exploited the weapon's range advantage and ammunition independence for perimeter security and extended patrol duty. Six-trooper teams could maintain operational readiness for longer periods without requiring ballistic munitions resupply.

Inner Sphere squads equipped with the Pulse Laser loadout deployed primarily in close-quarters and urban environments where the weapon's accuracy offset its limited range. Four-trooper teams used the configuration for building clearing and installation defense operations.

Nova Cat Points carrying the Pulse Laser configuration were assigned to urban garrison and close-defense roles within the Irece Prefecture. Five-trooper Points leveraged the pulse weapon's accuracy in the confined spaces of planetary installations and industrial complexes.

Level I units employing the Pulse Laser configuration deployed in facility defense and urban security operations where the weapon's precision targeting proved more valuable than range. Six-trooper formations could secure larger areas than standard five-trooper Points in defensive postures.

Inner Sphere organizations that acquired Thunderbird II suits deployed them in standard four-trooper squads. Republic Armed Forces units operating outside the Fortress Republic walls employed these squads alongside other battle armor types, leveraging the integrated C3 system to coordinate targeting data across mixed formations.

Clan Nova Cat expatriates serving within the Republic Armed Forces organized Thunderbird II suits into five-trooper Points, maintaining traditional Clan formation doctrine. These Points integrated the C3 networking capability with Clan tactical traditions, creating fire-linked teams that combined Clan aggression with Inner Sphere sensor sharing.

Republic Armed Forces Level I formations equipped with the Thunderbird II exploited the C3 system's full networking potential across six-trooper teams. The larger formation size maximized the number of sensors feeding the C3 network, making Level I deployments particularly effective in coordinated fire missions.

Inner Sphere forces organized captured or purchased G12 Tornado suits into standard four-trooper squads. Free Worlds League Military units received the largest share through sales from the Word of Blake, deploying them alongside conventional infantry for perimeter security, reconnaissance, and facility defense. Post-Jihad, Republic Armed Forces squads continued operating surplus G12s in garrison and security roles.

Republic of the Sphere formations drawing on Clan organizational traditions occasionally fielded G12 Tornado suits in five-trooper Points. Terra's continued production at Krupp Armament Works under Republic ownership ensured steady supply, and Point-sized teams proved effective for facility security and surveillance operations where the G12's stealth properties complemented the larger formation's coverage area.

The Word of Blake fielded G12 Tornado suits in six-trooper Level I formations as standard equipment for their marines and planetary security troops. Following the Schism, Blakist Level I teams wearing G12s spearheaded the seizure of Terra's orbital defense network during Operation Odysseus and helped secure the Titan Shipyards. The six-trooper formation gave Blakist commanders flexible small-unit teams for boarding actions, facility seizure, and garrison security throughout the Protectorate.

Inner Sphere squads equipped with the David light Gauss rifle configuration served as precision fire support elements, engaging targets at ranges beyond most battle armor weapons. Four-trooper squads typically operated as overwatch teams, providing accurate suppressive fire for advancing G12 or G13 teams during facility assaults and urban operations.

Five-trooper Points carrying the David light Gauss rifle configuration leveraged the weapon's extended range to establish overlapping fields of fire during defensive operations. Republic formations on Terra employed small numbers of these Points for perimeter security, where the precision weapon complemented the larger formation's ability to cover wider defensive sectors.

Word of Blake Level I formations armed with David light Gauss rifles served as dedicated marksman teams within larger Tornado detachments. The six-trooper structure allowed Blakist commanders to assign paired shooter-spotter teams across three positions, maximizing the weapon's precision engagement capability during facility defense and convoy escort operations.

Inner Sphere four-trooper squads carrying the flamer configuration specialized in building clearance and close-quarters operations where the weapon's area-effect damage proved decisive. FWLM and post-Jihad garrison forces valued flamer squads for riot control and anti-insurgency work in urban environments.

Five-trooper Points fielding the flamer configuration concentrated area-denial firepower for defensive operations. Republic units on Terra occasionally organized flamer-equipped Tornado operators into Points for installation security, where the larger formation size compensated for the weapon's limited range during perimeter defense.

Word of Blake Level I formations equipped with flamers served as assault and clearance teams aboard WarShips and space stations, where the weapon's effectiveness in confined spaces complemented the six-trooper formation's ability to secure multiple compartments simultaneously. Blakist marine detachments favored the flamer configuration for boarding actions and shipboard security duties.

Four-trooper Inner Sphere squads mounting heavy grenade launchers provided indirect fire support for mixed Tornado formations. The squad size allowed integration into standard infantry platoon structures, with grenade launcher teams delivering suppressive fire while other squads maneuvered into assault positions.

Five-trooper Points carrying heavy grenade launchers offered area suppression capability at the formation level. Republic forces organizing along Clan-influenced doctrine assigned grenade launcher Points to provide fire support within Stars alongside direct-fire Tornado configurations.

Word of Blake Level I formations armed with heavy grenade launchers served as fire support elements for larger Tornado detachments. The six-trooper structure maximized the volume of indirect fire available during facility assaults and defensive operations, with Blakist commanders using grenade launcher teams to suppress enemy positions ahead of close-assault elements.

Inner Sphere four-trooper squads equipped with machine guns served as general-purpose combat teams, providing sustained automatic fire for perimeter defense and convoy escort duties. The weapon's simplicity and conventional ammunition made it popular with garrison forces that lacked dedicated battle armor logistics chains.

Five-trooper Points mounting machine guns concentrated automatic firepower for area defense operations. Republic formations inherited machine gun-equipped G13s from post-Jihad salvage stocks on Terra, organizing them into Points for installation security where sustained fire capability outweighed precision engagement needs.

Word of Blake Level I formations carrying machine guns formed the backbone of Blakist marine security detachments. The six-trooper structure provided continuous automatic fire coverage for checkpoint operations, facility defense, and anti-insurgency patrols throughout the Protectorate, where the machine gun's sustained fire rate compensated for the Tornado's limited individual lethality.

Inner Sphere four-trooper squads fielding the small laser configuration operated as self-sufficient combat teams, free from ammunition resupply concerns that limited other G13 weapon loadouts. The energy weapon's reliability made these squads favored for extended patrol and garrison duties in remote postings.

Five-trooper Points equipped with small lasers provided sustained energy-weapon firepower without the logistical burden of ammunition resupply. Republic formations valued the configuration for independent patrol operations where the larger Point size and unlimited ammunition capacity allowed extended deployments away from supply lines.

Word of Blake Level I formations armed with small lasers served as rapid-response security teams, their energy weapons drawing power from the suit's internal systems without requiring ammunition stocks. Blakist commanders deployed laser-equipped Level I teams for shipboard security and space station defense, where ammunition storage constraints made energy weapons preferable to ballistic alternatives.

Inner Sphere four-trooper G14 squads served as forward logistics elements, carrying ammunition, medical supplies, and mission equipment alongside armed Tornado teams. The four-trooper squad offered sufficient cargo capacity to sustain a mixed Tornado formation through extended operations without conventional supply vehicles.

Five-trooper G14 Points assigned to Republic formations on Terra provided enhanced logistics capacity for Tornado Stars operating in urban and subterranean environments. The larger Point size increased the total cargo available per formation, supporting longer independent operations in areas inaccessible to conventional resupply.

Word of Blake Level I formations of G14 Tornado suits functioned as dedicated logistics teams embedded within larger Blakist Tornado detachments. Six operators carrying mission equipment provided substantial supply capacity for extended operations, enabling armed G12 and G13 teams to sustain engagements well beyond the range of conventional supply lines during Jihad-era campaigns.

Republic Armed Forces organized surviving G17 prototypes into four-trooper squads following the liberation of Terra. The suit's VTOL capability and advanced stealth made it valuable for special reconnaissance, though chronic maintenance difficulties and limited spare parts restricted operational deployments to high-priority missions.

Five-trooper Points of G17 Tornado suits remained theoretical given the extremely small number of prototypes produced. Republic formations with Clan-influenced organization may have grouped available G17s into partial Points for operational testing, though the suit's scarcity prevented meaningful fielding at any formation size beyond individual teams.

TerraSec developed the G17 for employment in six-trooper Level I formations consistent with Word of Blake military organization. Prototype G17 teams conducted raids against Coalition command and logistics facilities during the battle for Terra, their VTOL mobility and improved stealth allowing insertion across defensive lines that ground-based power armor could not penetrate. Coalition intelligence assessed that full-scale production would have made the liberation campaign significantly more costly.

text.capabilities: The original P12 Tornado combines basic stealth armor with an adaptive camouflage system that mimics combined visual, infrared, and electronic countermeasure concealment, allowing operators to approach targets undetected across most sensor bands. The suit's nearly 400-kilogram mass is supported entirely by the operator, permitting extended deployment without the energy signature of powered exoskeleton systems. A built-in heads-up display provides environmental data, low-light enhancement, and visual magnification, though some operators chose to forgo the helmet's protection for unimpeded sensory awareness. Two waist-mounted connection ports allow modified weapons to draw from the military power pack. Armored gloves enable infantry weapon use and anti-BattleMech attacks, though they can be removed for tasks requiring fine manual dexterity. The suit provides no mobility assistance beyond the operator's own speed.
text.deployment: Free Worlds League Military units organized their Tornado P12 suits into four-trooper squads following standard Inner Sphere infantry doctrine. Licensed production at Free Worlds Defense Industries on Gibson gave FWLM special operations teams direct access to the Tornado without relying on ComStar supply channels, though the suits remained reserved for sensitive reconnaissance and infiltration assignments rather than general infantry issue.

Very few P17 Hurricane suits reached Inner Sphere four-trooper squad organization. ComStar produced only a handful of the mixed-technology design, and any P17s organized into IS-standard squads likely represented post-Jihad redistribution of surviving suits to Republic or allied forces unfamiliar with ComStar formation doctrine.

The P17 Hurricane's extremely limited production makes five-trooper Point deployments speculative at best. Any such organization would have required assembling most of the known production run into a single formation. Republic forces inheriting ComStar assets may have experimented with Point-sized P17 teams, though no confirmed deployments exist in available records.

ComStar deployed the P17 Hurricane in its intended six-trooper Level I configuration as part of a dedicated hunter-killer Level II unit. The formation combined the P17's enhanced speed and ranged firepower with ComStar's established Level I tactical doctrine, creating a rapid-response team capable of tracking and eliminating high-value targets. Officially, only a handful of suits were produced, and the full strength of the P17 Level II remains classified.

Republic Armed Forces planners organized Tortoise II prototypes into four-trooper squads for initial evaluation, following standard Inner Sphere infantry doctrine. The aSRM configuration's balanced mix of missile and energy firepower made it a natural fit for general-purpose squad assignments during the 3134 field trials at Thetford Proving Grounds.

Five-trooper Points of the aSRM-equipped Tortoise II were allocated to Republic formations with Clan organizational heritage. The Point structure allowed concentrated missile firepower against hardened targets, with each additional trooper adding another salvo of advanced SRM fire to the formation's opening volley.

Six-trooper Level I formations of the aSRM variant were proposed for Republic units retaining ComStar-derived organizational structures. The larger formation size offered sustained engagement capability, with more troopers available to maintain fire while others repositioned or shed detachable weapon packs for increased mobility.

The C3 configuration's network coordination role made it particularly effective in four-trooper squads attached to combined-arms formations. Each squad could link with friendly BattleMechs and vehicles, improving targeting accuracy across the entire formation while the stealth armor helped the forward-deployed suits avoid detection.

Republic Points equipped with the C3 variant integrated into Clan-tradition combined-arms Stars, providing targeting data that enhanced the firepower of heavier assets. The five-trooper formation allowed broader network coverage across a Star's operational area, with each suit functioning as a forward sensor node.

Six-trooper Level I formations of the C3 configuration offered the most comprehensive battlefield networking capability. ComStar-derived Republic units employed the larger formation to blanket an operational zone with overlapping sensor coverage, creating a targeting web that made approaching forces visible to every networked friendly unit in the area.

Republic squads equipped with the LRM configuration served as organic fire support within four-trooper formations. The indirect fire capability allowed squads to engage from concealed positions, complementing faster battle armor units that could provide forward spotting data.

Five-trooper Points of LRM-equipped Tortoise IIs provided Clan-structured Republic formations with dedicated indirect fire assets. The Point organization concentrated enough long-range missile fire to suppress enemy positions or soften targets before faster elements closed to engagement range.

Level I formations of six LRM-armed troopers offered the deepest ammunition reserves and most sustained indirect fire capability of any Tortoise II deployment pattern. ComStar-tradition Republic units valued this configuration for defensive operations where sustained bombardment outweighed the need for rapid maneuver.

The SRM configuration's devastating close-range output suited the four-trooper squad format favored by Republic units with Inner Sphere infantry traditions. Squad-level doctrine emphasized coordinated volleys from the Clan SRM 6 launchers, concentrating fire to breach armored targets before closing to exploit openings with pulse laser fire.

Clan-organized Republic Points fielding the SRM variant leveraged the five-trooper formation for overwhelming alpha strikes. Five simultaneous SRM 6 volleys represented a staggering volume of fire for a battle armor formation, giving the Point raw striking power sufficient to threaten even medium-weight BattleMechs.

The PPC-armed upgrade gave Taurian four-trooper squads both improved survivability and energy-based ranged firepower without ammunition concerns. Squads equipped with this configuration were assigned to forward operating bases where sustained operations demanded self-sufficient infantry capable of engaging BattleMech targets at range and in close combat. The Taurian Defense Force prioritized this variant for units stationed along contested borders.

Five-trooper Points of PPC-armed upgraded Asterion suits remained uncommon, confined to small formations where Clan-pattern organization was adopted by Periphery forces. The energy weapon and improved close-combat suite combination made these Points functional in both ranged and swarming engagements, though logistics for the advanced armor components remained a persistent challenge outside Taurian territory.

Six-trooper Level I sections armed with the upgraded PPC Asterion provided Word of Blake formations with improved anti-BattleMech infantry during the latter stages of the Jihad. The combination of advanced armor, energy weaponry, and enhanced melee capability made these sections particularly dangerous in the close-quarters urban fighting that characterized many Jihad-era engagements.

Taurian Concordat Armed Forces organized their Asterion troopers into standard four-soldier squads, typically attached to combined-arms companies for garrison and border patrol duties. The rifle-armed configuration proved popular with Taurian quartermasters who valued its low maintenance burden and reliable ammunition supply. Squads operating along the Capellan and Federated Suns borders gained experience in anti-raider operations, where the Asterion's rugged simplicity outweighed its lack of advanced features.

Five-trooper Points of captured or salvaged Asterion suits saw limited use among Clan occupation forces in the Periphery border regions. Clan warriors regarded the design as crude but functional, and its straightforward maintenance profile made it easier to sustain without dedicated Clan technical support. These Points typically served in second-line garrison clusters where front-line Elemental suits were unavailable.

Word of Blake Militia formations occasionally fielded Asterion suits acquired through Capellan trade channels, organizing them into six-trooper Level I sections consistent with ComStar military doctrine. These formations supplemented Blakist infantry divisions during the Jihad, particularly in rear-area security roles where the Asterion's conventional armor and ballistic armament were sufficient for the operational requirements.

The energy weapon configuration found particular favor among Taurian units deployed to remote frontier garrisons where ammunition resupply was difficult to guarantee. Four-trooper squads equipped with the support PPC variant could maintain combat effectiveness for extended periods without logistical support, a critical advantage along the Concordat's thinly defended borders. Several Taurian Defense Force regiments standardized on this configuration for their battle armor detachments.

Clan-sized Points of PPC-armed Asterion suits appeared in limited numbers among garrison forces operating in former Periphery territories. The energy weapon configuration's independence from ammunition supply chains made it marginally more attractive to Clan logisticians accustomed to self-sufficient Point operations. These formations remained uncommon, assigned primarily to isolated postings where resupply schedules were unreliable.

ComStar and Word of Blake Level I formations occasionally incorporated PPC-armed Asterion suits into their infantry organizations. The six-trooper sections provided energy-based fire support within combined-arms Level II groupings, supplementing heavier assets during security operations. The configuration's ammunition independence aligned well with Com Guard logistical preferences for self-contained tactical units.

The Magistracy of Canopus adopted the Theseus as its primary battle armor platform, organizing troopers into four-soldier squads within the MAF's conventional infantry structure. The Canopians named their variant after the legendary founder of Athens who slew the Minotaur, a deliberate political provocation directed at their Taurian allies. Canopian squads served across the Magistracy's territories, with particular concentrations along the Marian Hegemony border and in colonial defense garrisons.

Captured Theseus suits organized into five-trooper Points saw occasional use among Clan-aligned forces operating near the Periphery. The design's functional equivalence to the Asterion meant that Clan warriors who encountered either variant found them interchangeable in combat performance, though the Canopian aesthetic styling was sometimes remarked upon with bemusement by Clan Elementals more accustomed to purpose-built Clan hardware.

ComStar Militia and Word of Blake infantry divisions organized Theseus suits into six-trooper Level I sections when quantities were available through trade with the Magistracy. These formations filled gaps in Blakist infantry tables of organization during the Jihad, providing basic battle armor capability to divisions that could not be equipped with more advanced designs from Word of Blake's own production facilities.

CCAF experimental formations tested the BC3-equipped Ying Long in four-trooper squads networked into C3 lances alongside BattleMechs and vehicles. The targeting data shared through the C3 computer allowed the squad's light gauss rifles to achieve accuracy beyond what individual troopers could manage independently. Production remained limited to a small number of prototype suits evaluated by front-line units during the closing stages of the Jihad.

The plasma rifle's incendiary properties proved useful during operations where area denial was as important as direct casualties.

Five-trooper Points of Ying Long suits were extremely rare, limited to isolated instances where Clan-aligned forces acquired small numbers of the mimetic-armored suits through battlefield salvage. The camouflage technology attracted interest from Clan scientists, but the Inner Sphere manufacturing base and exotic armor type made sustained Point-level operations impractical without a dedicated Capellan supply chain.

Word of Blake forces had a natural affinity for the Ying Long, given that its mimetic armor derived from technology first employed on the Blakist Purifier. Six-trooper Level I sections of Ying Long suits complemented existing Blakist battle armor formations during the Jihad. The larger section size allowed Blakist commanders to deploy mimetic-equipped troopers in overlapping fields of observation, creating sensor nets that conventional detection equipment struggled to penetrate.

text.deployment: Inner Sphere forces first encountered the Undine through Clan Diamond Shark trade networks following the Jihad. Four-trooper squads organized in standard Inner Sphere fashion deployed the suit for coastal defense and underwater facility security operations. The Federated Suns proved the most enthusiastic Inner Sphere adopter, studying captured and purchased Undines closely enough to develop their own amphibious battle armor program.

Goliath Scorpion Points of Undine troopers excelled in defensive underwater Trials, leveraging the suit's aquatic mobility and amphibious armament to dominate engagements on their own terms. Five-trooper Points operated primarily from underwater facilities on Scorpion-held worlds, conducting patrols, defending mineral extraction sites, and securing naval installations against rival Clan incursions.

Six-trooper formations of Undine suits saw limited adoption outside standard Clan organization. Those units that fielded the suit in oversized formations did so to maximize underwater patrol coverage, using the additional troopers to establish wider security perimeters around critical submarine infrastructure and deep-sea industrial sites.

The Upgrade variant's land mobility opened the Undine to broader Inner Sphere adoption. Four-trooper squads employed the suit as a light fire support element, pairing it with heavier battle armor in combined-arms formations. The jump-capable Upgrade proved far more attractive to Inner Sphere militaries than the aquatic-only base model, offering genuine tactical flexibility on conventional battlefields.

Goliath Scorpion Points fielded the Upgrade alongside standard Elemental formations for combined ground operations. The Upgrade's matching jump range allowed it to keep pace with Elemental Points while providing LRM fire support, a capability the heavier suit lacked. This complementary pairing of Elementals and Undine Upgrades became a common Scorpion tactical formation for operations where underwater capability was unnecessary.

Six-trooper formations using the Upgrade variant offered conventional land combat capability that the aquatic base model could not provide. These larger formations were occasionally fielded by Clan garrison units that acquired the suits through trade but lacked the underwater infrastructure to exploit the original Undine's strengths, making the land-capable Upgrade their only practical option.

Draconis Combine Admiralty marine squads employ the DCA configuration in four-trooper teams aboard WarShips, DropShips, and orbital installations. These squads specialize in boarding actions and shipboard security, exploiting the variant's close-quarters focus to control corridors and compartments during contested engagements.

Clan Nova Cat naval assets occasionally deploy DCA-pattern Voids in five-trooper Points for shipboard defense and boarding operations. The configuration's emphasis on close combat aligns with Clan boarding doctrine, though Nova Cat warriors more commonly favor their own Gauss-equipped configuration for general surface operations.

ComStar and Word of Blake naval personnel who acquired DCA-pattern Voids organized them into six-trooper Level I marine detachments. The configuration's shipboard optimization made it a useful addition to Com Guard vessel security, though availability remained extremely limited outside Combine space.

Clan Nova Cat forces did not receive the Minelayer variant, as the Combine's Procurement Department chose to withhold production-grade minelayers from the Clan enclaves. This exclusion reflected deteriorating relations between the DCMS and the Nova Cats, and the Minelayer's reduced frame size, which dropped accommodation for Elemental-sized operators, further limited its utility in Clan Points.

Six-trooper Level I formations using the Minelayer configuration could establish significantly wider minefields than smaller squad sizes, leveraging the additional troopers to cover broader frontages. Few units outside the Combine operated the variant, and the Level I organizational option remained largely theoretical given the Minelayer's near-exclusive DCMS availability.

Inner Sphere forces that obtained Nova Cat-pattern Voids through trade or salvage organized them into standard four-trooper squads. The MagShot Gauss rifle's performance made this configuration attractive to DCMS commanders who valued ranged precision, and limited numbers entered service with regular Combine infantry formations.

Clan Nova Cat warriors field this configuration in standard five-trooper Points, where the MagShot Gauss rifle and vibro battle claw combination complements the aggressive close-range tactics favored by Clan infantry doctrine. Second-line garrison clusters received the majority of Nova Cat-pattern Voids across the Irece Prefecture.

The rare ComStar or Word of Blake formations that operated Nova Cat-pattern Voids organized them into six-trooper Level I units. The configuration's Clan-derived Gauss technology made it a high-value salvage target, and captured examples were studied for intelligence purposes as much as fielded in combat.

Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery units organize their Void troopers into four-trooper squads following standard Inner Sphere infantry doctrine. These squads typically operate alongside BattleMech lances, providing reconnaissance and anti-infantry screening. DCMS elite formations such as the Otomo and the Genyosha brigades received priority allocation during the suit's initial production run.

Clan Nova Cat warriors deploy the Void in standard five-trooper Points, integrating them into Stars alongside OmniMechs. The suit's accommodation for Elemental-sized operators made it one of the few Inner Sphere designs that Nova Cat warriors willingly adopted, with Points serving primarily in garrison and second-line formations across the Irece Prefecture.

ComStar and Word of Blake forces that acquired Void suits organized them into six-trooper Level I formations per their standard military doctrine. These units saw limited deployment given the suit's near-exclusive availability within the Draconis Combine, with most examples reaching Com Guard or Militia hands through battlefield salvage or clandestine procurement.

Inner Sphere commands fielding the Reactive variant organized their troopers into standard four-member squads. The improved survivability of the reactive armor made these smaller squads more durable under fire, partially offsetting the reduced numbers compared to larger Clan Point formations.

ComStar and Word of Blake Level I formations equipped with the Reactive variant gained significant staying power in defensive engagements. Six troopers mounting reactive armor created formidable fixed-position units capable of absorbing sustained punishment while maintaining effective counter-fire against both armored and conventional threats.

Inner Sphere military formations organizing captured or traded Warg suits operated them in four-trooper squads, following standard infantry doctrine. These smaller formations proved adequate for defensive assignments where the Warg's limited mobility was less of a handicap, though fewer suits per squad reduced the concentrated firepower that made the design effective in fixed-position engagements.

Clan Wolf Points of five Warg troopers formed the primary tactical deployment of the suit. Assigned to support frontline OmniMech formations, these Points typically rode into battle aboard Badger or Bandit armored personnel carriers before dismounting to establish defensive positions. The five-trooper Point maximized the suit's combined missile volleys, creating overlapping fields of fire that could stall even heavy BattleMech advances.

ComStar and Word of Blake formations organized Warg suits into six-trooper Level I units when examples became available through salvage or trade. The larger formation size compensated for the suit's slow speed by concentrating more firepower at a single defensive point, aligning with Com Guard doctrine that emphasized holding fixed positions with overwhelming local superiority.

text.overview: The Water Elemental mining suit was a sophisticated submersible exoskeleton developed by Clan Goliath Scorpion for deep-sea industrial operations. Produced at the Hades Industrial Complex on Dagda beginning around 2842, the medium-weight design gave its operators the strength, mobility, and environmental protection needed for underwater mineral extraction and construction work at extreme depths. Though conceived as a purely civilian tool, the Water Elemental proved to be the most consequential industrial development in Clan history, providing the technical and engineering foundation from which all Clan battle armor would eventually descend.
text.capabilities:
Powered by myomer musculature and sealed against extreme underwater pressure, the Water Elemental mining suit achieved its remarkable performance through a network of synchronized micro thrusters linked to thousands of pressure sensors woven into the inner lining. Simple gestures from the operator translated into precise thrust commands, allowing the suit to reach speeds rivaling dedicated submersible transports. The thruster array could also lock the suit motionless against strong currents, enabling precision work in turbulent conditions. Additional buoyancy control devices and depth sensors prevented dangerous rapid ascents while monitoring remaining power and air supply.

As a purely industrial design, the suit carried no weapons. Its equipment loadout included cutting torches, an industrial drill, a basic manipulator for material handling, and a searchlight for low-visibility operations. Two hundred kilograms of standard armor protected the operator from environmental hazards, though this protection was never intended to withstand directed weapons fire. On land, the suit managed only modest walking speed, with its design optimized entirely for underwater mobility.
text.deployment: Five-trooper Points formed the standard configuration for Goliath Scorpion underwater mining operations. Deployed from the Hades Industrial Complex on Dagda, these crews worked mineral extraction sites across Scorpion-held worlds. The Point structure provided sufficient manpower for heavy excavation work and built-in redundancy, ensuring that the loss of a single operator would not halt a critical deep-sea operation.
text.battleHistory:
Clan Goliath Scorpion's extensive underwater holdings demanded specialized equipment for deep-sea mineral extraction and construction. Around 2842, Scorpion scientists at the Hades Industrial Complex on Dagda produced the Water Elemental mining suit, a submersible exoskeleton that gave its operators far greater capability than any conventional diving apparatus. The suit's powered frame allowed workers to perform complex underwater tasks at depths and durations previously impossible. The Scorpions treated these suits as unremarkable industrial tools, deploying them across their underwater mining colonies with little thought to military applications.

That changed around 2860, when visiting Clan Wolf forces on Dagda learned of the Scorpions' mining programs and the exoskeletons powering them. A Wolf Star Captain, recognizing the suits' combat potential, issued a Trial of Possession for one of the units. Point Commander Sarah, assigned the defense, chose her ground carefully. She selected nearby wetlands featuring deep waterways, aggressive fauna, and treacherous footing. Clan Wolf bid a Star of jump infantry against Scorpion operators in their mining suits. Sarah exploited the terrain to devastating effect, using the Water Elementals' aquatic mobility to isolate and eliminate the Wolf warriors piecemeal. The Scorpions lost only a single pilot in the engagement.

Despite the Trial's outcome, Clan Wolf remained determined to acquire the technology. Through merchant caste trade channels, the Wolves obtained Water Elemental suits and began studying their military potential. Engineers added armor plating, jump jets, and weapon mounts to the basic exoskeleton frame. By 2868, these modifications produced a functional combat suit that Clan Wolf first deployed against the Nova Cats. The Elemental battle armor had been born, a design that would reshape Clan warfare for centuries. Clan Hell's Horses subsequently won the technology through Trials of their own, bringing their genetically bred Elemental phenotype warriors into the partnership of suit and soldier that defined Clan powered infantry.

The mining suit's influence extended far beyond the Elemental itself. While Clan Wolf pursued a general-purpose combat design, the specialist prototypes developed during early weaponization experiments inspired an entire family of role-specific suits. The Gnome, Salamander, Sylph, and Undine each traced their conceptual lineage back to those early variants, with the Undine being the most direct descendant of the original underwater design.

Throughout these developments, the Goliath Scorpions continued producing Water Elemental suits at the Hades Industrial Complex for their original mining purpose. Star Commander Vikram demonstrated the unmodified suits' latent combat potential during the Golden Century, pressing a Star of Water Elementals into service on Circe against Clan Mongoose in an unusual underwater engagement. Armed only with industrial tools against scuba infantry, Vikram's forces won a hard-fought battle in flooded terrain, with fierce currents and the exoskeletons' bulk proving as deadly as any weapon. Production at the Hades Industrial Complex continued under Goliath Scorpion control through the Jihad era. Following the Wars of Reaving, Clan Star Adder absorbed Scorpion holdings in the Homeworlds, and the Dagda facilities passed to new management, though the mining suits continued to serve their original industrial purpose.

text.deployment: Four-trooper Anti-Infantry squads serve in Dominion formations organized along Inner Sphere lines, where the smaller squad size allows tighter coordination during building-clearing and urban sweep operations. The reduced headcount concentrates the squad's improved sensor capability into a more manageable element for freeborn infantry officers accustomed to conventional fire-team tactics.
text.battleHistory:
The Wraith traces its lineage to the Rogue Bear, a heavy battle armor prototype first fielded by Clan Ghost Bear garrison forces in the early 3070s. Decades of iterative refinement at BA Facility Gamma on Mannedorf transformed the concept into the production Wraith, which entered Rasalhague Dominion service in 3116. Unlike most Clan battle armor, the Wraith was engineered around interchangeable form factors to accommodate the Dominion's mixed Clan-freeborn military, where standardized Elemental-proportioned suits excluded many otherwise capable warriors from powered armor duty. Quartermasters complained that the variety of frame sizes created a logistical burden, but field commanders valued the expanded recruitment pool.

The Wraith earned its reputation during operations in the late 3130s. text.deployment: Marik-Stewart Commonwealth forces organized their Xiphos troopers into standard four-trooper squads, integrating them into combined-arms formations alongside BattleMech lances and conventional infantry platoons. The A configuration’s balanced ballistic loadout made it a favored general-purpose assignment for garrison and defensive units, with squads frequently paired to provide mutual fire support during territorial defense operations.

Following the capture of Washburn’s production facilities, Clan Wolf organized Xiphos suits into standard five-trooper Points. The A configuration’s straightforward ballistic armament appealed to Wolf warriors who valued reliable firepower, and Points equipped with this loadout saw action during the Wolf Empire’s continued expansion, including raids against the Republic Remnant on Alhena where Wolf warriors adopted Commonwealth ambush tactics with mixed results.

Six-trooper formations of the Xiphos occasionally appeared in units with non-standard organizational structures, where commanders grouped additional troopers for increased firepower density. The A configuration’s ammunition-dependent weapons benefited from the larger formation’s ability to sustain fire across extended engagements, though such formations remained uncommon outside of garrison and militia assignments.

Commonwealth four-trooper squads equipped with the B configuration specialized in anti-vehicle and anti-BattleMech operations. These squads were often held in reserve during defensive engagements, deploying forward once enemy armor committed to the assault. The plasma rifle’s heat-inducing effects proved effective at disrupting vehicle crews and forcing BattleMech pilots into difficult thermal management during close-quarters fighting.

Clan Wolf Points fielding the B configuration used the plasma weaponry in close-quarters engagements where its heat-generating effects could be exploited against Inner Sphere opponents. Wolf warriors, accustomed to heat-intensive combat in OmniMechs, adapted quickly to directing plasma fire against enemy armor and fortifications during conquest operations across the former Free Worlds League.

The B configuration’s plasma and missile armament occasionally appeared in six-trooper formations assigned to perimeter defense and area denial roles. The larger formation provided additional thermal firepower, useful for deterring vehicle advances and creating zones of intense heat that disrupted enemy movement through confined areas and chokepoints.

Four-trooper squads equipped with the C configuration served in dedicated reconnaissance and clearing roles within Commonwealth combined-arms formations. The heat sensor gave squad leaders valuable threat detection capability, while the heavy flamer provided decisive firepower for clearing fortified positions and dense terrain that heavier units could not easily access.

Wolf Points equipped with the C configuration served as screening elements for larger formations. The heat sensor’s ability to detect concealed defenders complemented Clan assault doctrine, allowing Points to identify ambush positions before the main force committed. Wolf commanders valued the configuration for its ability to reduce casualties during planetary assaults against prepared Inner Sphere defenders.

Six-trooper formations with the C configuration were occasionally deployed for area clearance operations in urban and industrial environments. The additional troopers allowed systematic sweeps of large facilities or dense terrain, with pairs alternating between sensor scanning and flamer engagement to ensure thorough coverage of assigned sectors.

The C3 Zou saw its heaviest four-trooper deployment within the DCMS's most active combat commands. The Sword of Light and New Samarkand Regulars adopted the suit to replace older heavy battle armor, pairing squads with lighter Kishi teams along the Davion border. During the assault on Palmyra, the Seventh New Samarkand Regulars used a Zou squad as a central observation post, coordinating fire that helped turn back the Fifth Ceti Hussars' flanking maneuver through the Yorkville Pass.

Organizations fielding five-trooper formations could leverage the C3 Zou's coordination capabilities across a larger tactical element. The additional trooper allowed the formation to maintain C3 network coverage even after taking casualties, preserving the squad's command-and-control function under fire. The heavier formation proved well-suited to defensive operations where maintaining network integrity outweighed individual mobility.

Six-trooper formations equipped with the C3 Zou gained substantial coordination capacity, with the larger unit able to maintain overlapping sensor coverage and fire direction across a wider frontage. The additional troopers provided both redundancy for the C3 network and increased close-defense capability, allowing the formation to anchor larger combined-arms elements while remaining difficult to neutralize through attrition.

Inner Sphere infantry doctrine organized standard Zou troopers into four-member squads for garrison and area denial operations within the DCMS. The configuration's straightforward armament required minimal logistical support, making it practical for lower-threat postings. One well-known example is the White Zou of the Fourth Dieron Regulars, an individual suit considered a regimental mascot. Since its arrival in 3127, the Fourth has lost every battle the White Zou participated in, and soldiers believe the curse can only break when the armor is destroyed in combat.

Military organizations employing five-trooper formations could field the standard Zou in a configuration suited to their doctrinal requirements. The additional trooper increased aggregate firepower and survivability, allowing the formation to absorb casualties while maintaining combat effectiveness. The Zou's heavy armor and intuitive controls made it adaptable to organizational structures beyond its original four-trooper design.

Forces organized around six-trooper formations gained additional tactical depth when fielding the standard Zou. The larger formation allowed commanders to assign specialized roles within the unit, with some troopers providing suppressive fire while others advanced on objectives. The suit's durability and low sensor signature made it effective in these larger groupings, where concentrated firepower could compensate for limited mobility.
